# LLMock — reference for coding agents

> `llmock` is a local HTTP server that imitates LLM APIs (OpenAI chat completions, Anthropic Messages, Gemini generateContent, OpenAI embeddings) with generated or canned replies. Use it so an app or test suite can run without a real provider. This file is the compact reference for agents wiring llmock into a project; README.md is the human tutorial.

Describes the llmock version this file ships with (read it from `node_modules/llmock/llms.txt`). Node >= 20 (tested on 24 LTS). Nothing here needs an API key or network access.

## Mental model

- One server process serves **one preset** (a named entry in `.llmockrc.json` → `models`). A preset fixes the chat route, the wire format, and the reply behaviour. To mock two providers at once, run two servers on two ports.
- Config is read once at startup. Any change to `.llmockrc.json` needs `stop` + `start`. Fixture files and the stored responses file are re-read on every request, so editing them needs no restart. Response rules, chaos settings and the response delay can also be changed on a running server over HTTP (see Admin API); nothing else can be changed without a restart.
- No auth: API keys and headers are ignored (SDKs still need a non-empty dummy key).
- Replies are text only. There are no tool calls and no token counting endpoint. Failures (an HTTP error, or a stream that fails part-way through) are simulated only with `chaos` on (see Chaos). A reply ends normally unless its response rule sets `stopReason` (see Fixture replies).

## Run it

```bash
npm install --save-dev llmock
npx llmock start --model=claude        # detached; returns once the server answers
npx llmock start --model=claude --foreground   # attached; use in Docker/CI or to see errors
npx llmock stop                        # add --port=<n> if not 8001
```

- Detached `start` waits until the server answers, then exits 0. It exits 1 if the server fails to start (the server's output is not attached: rerun with `--foreground` to see the error) or if a server already answers on that port.
- With `--foreground` the command never returns; poll for readiness yourself: `GET /ping` → `200 {"response":"server is running"}`.
- Confirm what is live: `GET /ui-meta` → JSON with `version` (llmock version), `llmName`, `llmUrlEndpoint`, `serverPort`, `streamingStatus`, `validateRequests`, delays.
- `stop` kills whatever process is listening on the port (default 8001, it does not read the config). Do not point it at a port another service uses.
- Run the CLI from the folder containing `.llmockrc.json`, or set `CONFIG_PATH=<path>` (relative to the cwd).
- Scaffold alternative: `npm create llmock@latest <dir>` creates a standalone folder (config, Docker files, npm scripts). It prompts interactively if `<dir>` is omitted or already exists. Its scripts: `npm run llmock:start`, `llmock:stop`, `llmock:<preset>`. Its Docker setup mounts only `.llmockrc.json`; templates, fixtures and a stored responses file are copied into the image, so changing them needs `npm run docker:rebuild` (or an added volume).

## Point a client at it (default port 8001)

| Client | Preset | Setting |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic SDK | `claude` | `baseURL: "http://localhost:8001"`, `apiKey: "mock"` (or env `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`). SDK calls `POST /v1/messages`. |
| OpenAI SDK / LangChain `ChatOpenAI` | `chatgpt` | `baseURL: "http://localhost:8001/chatgpt"`, `apiKey: "mock"`. SDK calls `POST /chatgpt/chat/completions`. |
| OpenAI SDK, chat + embeddings on one base URL | custom | Set the preset `endpoint` to `"v1/chat/completions"` and use `baseURL: "http://localhost:8001/v1"`. |
| Gemini-style REST | `gemini` | `POST http://localhost:8001/models/gemini-pro:generateContent` |
| Raw HTTP | any | `POST http://localhost:8001/<endpoint>` with `Content-Type: application/json` |

Embeddings are always at `/v1/embeddings`, not under the chat prefix: with the stock `chatgpt` preset an OpenAI client using base `…/chatgpt` will 404 on embeddings.

## `.llmockrc.json`

Looked up in the cwd. If absent, built-in defaults are used (presets `chatgpt`, `gemini`, `streaming`, `embeddings`, `claude`; note `chatgpt`/`gemini`/`streaming` default to a 3000–5000 ms delay). If present it **replaces** the defaults entirely; nothing is merged.

```json
{
  "defaultModel": "claude",
  "models": {
    "claude": {
      "name": "claude",
      "model": "claude-opus-5-5",
      "endpoint": "v1/messages",
      "responseType": "lorem",
      "maxLoremParas": 4,
      "validateRequests": false,
      "logRequests": true,
      "debug": false,
      "stream": false,
      "responseDelay": { "min": 0, "max": 0 },
      "embeddings": { "enabled": false, "dimensions": 128 },
      "responseRules": [
        { "match": "Classify this ticket", "file": "fixtures/triage.json" }
      ]
    }
  },
  "server": { "port": 8001, "host": "0.0.0.0" }
}
```

Only `name` and `endpoint` are required in a preset. The Default column applies to fields omitted from a preset in your file (the built-in presets set their own values).

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defaultModel` | string | `chatgpt` | Preset used when `--model` is not given. |
| `models.<preset>.name` | string | required | Wire format: `"openai"`, `"gemini"`, `"claude"`, or the name of your own templates (see Custom formats). `"claude"` also switches on Anthropic-specific behaviour. |
| `model` | string | `mock-model` | Informational. Only the claude format uses it (fallback when the request has no `model`). |
| `endpoint` | string | required | Chat route, no leading slash. Registered for both POST and GET. Must not be `v1/embeddings` while embeddings are enabled (startup error). |
| `responseType` | `"lorem"` \| `"stored"` | `lorem` | `lorem`: 1..`maxLoremParas` random sentences. `stored`: random pick from the preset's `storedResponsesFile`, or from 11 fixed strings bundled in the package when that is unset. Any other value: 1–10 lorem paragraphs. |
| `maxLoremParas` | number | 8 | Max **sentences** for `lorem`. |
| `validateRequests` | boolean | false | See Validation. |
| `logRequests` | boolean | false | Record the most recent validated requests (shown at `GET /ui-request-log`). |
| `maxLoggedRequests` | number | 10 | How many requests the log keeps. Capped at 100; a value below 1 or not a number falls back to 10. |
| `debug` | boolean | false | Verbose console output. |
| `stream` | boolean | false | SSE for `openai`/`gemini` formats. Ignored by `claude`. |
| `responseDelay.min/max` | ms | 0 / 0 | Random wait before each reply. `0`/`0` disables. |
| `embeddings.enabled` | boolean | false | Registers `/v1/embeddings`. When false the route 404s. |
| `embeddings.dimensions` | number | 128 | Default vector length. |
| `responseRules` | `{match, file, stopReason?}[]`, `{match, files, stopReason?}[]`, `{match, text, stopReason?}[]` or `{match, fail}[]` | none | See Fixture replies. A rule with `fail` fails the calls that match it. |
| `storedResponsesFile` | string | none | JSON file of texts for `responseType: "stored"`. See Stored replies. |
| `chaos.enabled` | boolean | false | Fail some calls. See Chaos. |
| `chaos.frequency` | integer ≥ 1 | 1 | Fail 1 in this many calls. `1` fails every call. |
| `chaos.mode` | `"every"` \| `"random"` | `every` | `every`: calls X, 2X, 3X… fail (deterministic). `random`: each call fails with probability 1/X. |
| `chaos.status` | 400–599 | 500 | HTTP status of the error. With `kind: "stream-error"` it picks the error type sent in the stream. |
| `chaos.kind` | `"http"` \| `"stream-error"` \| `"stream-drop"` \| `"stream-stall"` | `http` | What a failing call gets: an HTTP error, or a stream that starts and then errors, is cut, or goes silent. |
| `chaos.afterChunks` | integer ≥ 0 | 2 | Content deltas a failing stream sends before a `stream-*` kind fails it. |
| `server.port` | number | 8001 | Listen port. |
| `server.host` | string | `0.0.0.0` | Bind address. Use `127.0.0.1` to keep the mock off the network; keep `0.0.0.0` in Docker. |
| `server.admin` | boolean | true | `false` leaves the `/admin/*` routes out (see Admin API). |
| `server.uiTheme` | `"dark"` \| `"light"` | `dark` | Dashboard colours only; no effect on the API. Also set by the `UI_THEME` environment variable (wins over the config; `--uiTheme` wins over both). Any other value means `dark`. Reported as `uiTheme` by `GET /ui-meta`. |

CLI flags override the selected preset for one run: `--model --port --host --admin --uiTheme --endpoint --responseType --maxLoremParas --validateRequests --logRequests --maxLoggedRequests --debug --stream --delayMin --delayMax --chaos --chaosFrequency --chaosMode --chaosStatus --chaosKind --chaosAfterChunks --embeddings --embeddingDimensions --foreground`. Both `--key=value` and `--key value` work. Booleans must be the literal `true`/`false`; every flag except `--foreground` needs a value.

## Fixture replies (`responseRules`)

The way to get deterministic output, e.g. JSON your code parses.

- A rule fires when `match` occurs as a **case-sensitive substring** of any string value anywhere in the request body: every message of every turn, the system prompt, content blocks, and also values like `model` and `role`. Keys are not searched.
- First matching rule in array order wins. Put specific rules first and use distinctive markers (`"user"` would match every request).
- Because earlier turns are searched, a rule that matched turn 1 keeps matching all later turns of that conversation.
- The reply text is the file's bytes, verbatim, including a trailing newline. It is inserted as the assistant message text in the preset's normal envelope (and streamed if streaming applies); it is not the raw HTTP body.
- `file` resolves relative to the folder containing the config file.
- Random variety for one kind of request: give the rule `files` instead of `file`, e.g. `{ "match": "Summarise", "files": ["fixtures/a.txt", "fixtures/b.txt"] }`. One file is picked at random on each matching request. A rule has `file` or `files`, not both.
- Inline reply: give the rule `text` instead of a file, e.g. `{ "match": "Classify", "text": "{\"priority\":\"high\"}" }`. The reply text is that string, verbatim (`""` is an empty reply). A rule has only one of `text`, `file`, `files`.
- No rule matched → normal `responseType` reply.
- How the reply ends: add `stopReason` to a rule (with `file` or `files`) to stand for a truncated or refused reply, e.g. `{ "match": "Summarise this", "file": "fixtures/cut-off.txt", "stopReason": "max_tokens" }`. Values: `end` (the default: a normal end), `max_tokens`, `refusal`. The Responses section lists what each becomes on the wire. The reply text is still the file's bytes: llmock does not shorten it, so write a fixture that looks cut off (or, for a refusal, whatever text your app should see).
- Failing one prompt: give a rule `fail` and every call that matches it fails, whether or not `chaos` is on, while every other call is left alone. E.g. `{ "match": "Summarise the Q3 report", "fail": { "kind": "stream-error", "status": 529, "afterChunks": 1 } }`.
  - `fail` is an object with three optional settings that mean what they mean in `chaos`: `kind` (default `http`), `status` (default 500), `afterChunks` (default 2). `"fail": {}` is an HTTP 500. The rule's settings are its own: nothing is taken from the preset's `chaos`.
  - What the call gets is exactly what a failing chaos call of that `kind` gets (see Chaos): the same error bodies, the same `x-llmock-chaos: true` header, the same handling of a call that did not ask for a stream.
  - `file`/`files` are optional on a rule with `fail`. They only matter to a `stream-*` kind, as the text the stream sends before it fails; with neither, that text is the normal `responseType` reply. `stopReason` is never reached.
  - The rule fails every time it matches, so a client that retries the same prompt fails again. To have a retry succeed, use `chaos` with `frequency: 2` instead.
  - A call failed by a rule is added to `chaosInjected` but is not counted as a chaos call, so it does not shift which of the other calls `chaos` fails. The first matching rule still wins, so put a `fail` rule above a broader rule it overlaps with.
- `match` or `file` empty/non-string, `text` not a string, `files` not a non-empty array of non-empty strings, more than one of `text`, `file` and `files` set, none set on a rule without `fail`, a `stopReason` other than those three, or a `fail` that is not an object or has an unknown `kind`, a `status` outside 400–599 or an `afterChunks` that is not an integer ≥ 0 → server refuses to start. File missing → startup warning (every entry of `files` is checked), and a matching request that picks it gets `500` (no fallback to lorem).
- GET requests have no body, so rules never apply to them.
- `GET /ui-meta` → `responseRules` lists the active rules in match order as `{"id", "source", "match", "text", "files": [...], "stopReason", "fail"}` (`source` is `"runtime"` for a rule added through the Admin API, which is listed first and has an `id`, else `"config"` with `id: null`; `text` is `null` unless the rule has one; a single `file` is reported as a one-entry `files`, no fixture as `[]`; a rule with no `stopReason` reports `"end"`; `fail` is `null`, or `{"kind", "status", "afterChunks"}` with the defaults filled in).
- `GET /ui-rule-file?rule=<i>&file=<j>` → `{"match", "file", "content"}` for file `j` of config rule `i` (both zero-based; `i` counts the config file's rules only, so rules added through the admin API do not shift it). Unknown position → `404`; unreadable file → `500` with `{"error"}`.

## Admin API (`/admin/*`)

The way to set up a reply or a failure from inside a test, with no fixture file, no config edit and no restart. Changes made here live in memory only: the config file is never written and a restart drops them.

| Route | Body | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /admin/rules` | none | `200 {"rules": [...]}`: every active rule in match order, in the `responseRules` shape of `GET /ui-meta` |
| `POST /admin/rules` | `{"match", "text"?, "stopReason"?, "fail"?, "times"?}` | `201 {"rule": {...}}` with its `id` (`"r1"`, `"r2"`…); `400 {"error"}` if not valid (nothing is added) |
| `DELETE /admin/rules/<id>` | none | `200 {"rules": [...]}`; `404 {"error"}` for an unknown id |
| `DELETE /admin/rules` | none | `200 {"rules": [...]}`: runtime rules removed, config rules kept |
| `GET /admin/chaos` | none | `200 {"chaos": {"enabled", "frequency", "mode", "status", "kind", "afterChunks"}, "stats": {"calls", "injected"}}` |
| `PATCH /admin/chaos` | any of `{"enabled", "frequency", "mode", "status", "kind", "afterChunks"}` | `200` in the `GET /admin/chaos` shape; `400 {"error"}` if not valid (nothing is changed) |
| `GET /admin/delay` | none | `200 {"delay": {"min", "max"}}` (ms) |
| `PATCH /admin/delay` | `{"min"?, "max"?}` (ms) | `200 {"delay": {"min", "max"}}`; `400 {"error"}` if not valid (nothing is changed) |
| `GET /admin/settings` | none | `200 {"settings": {"responseType", "maxLoremParas", "stream", "validateRequests", "logRequests", "maxLoggedRequests"}}` |
| `PATCH /admin/settings` | any of those six keys | `200` in the `GET /admin/settings` shape; `400 {"error"}` if not valid (nothing is changed) |
| `POST /admin/reset` | none | `200 {"rules", "chaos", "stats", "delay", "settings"}`: runtime rules removed, chaos, delay and reply settings back to their startup values (config file plus CLI flags), chaos counts back to 0 |

- `match`, `stopReason` and `fail` mean exactly what they mean in `responseRules` (see Fixture replies). A rule needs `text` or `fail`; with both, `text` is what a `stream-*` failure sends before it fails.
- `file` and `files` are refused with `400`: the reply must be `text`. Any other key is refused too.
- `times` (integer ≥ 1, runtime rules only; a `times` in the config file's `responseRules` is ignored): the rule answers that many matching requests, then removes itself. Omitted → the rule stays until removed or reset. Each matching request the rule replies to or fails (its own `fail`) counts once; a request that chaos fails does not count, so the rule is still there for the retry. A listing shows the requests left as `times` (`null` for a rule that stays and for config rules). Fail once then succeed: `{"match": "X", "fail": {"status": 529}, "times": 1}`. A reply per call in turn: add `{"match": "X", "text": "first", "times": 1}` then `{"match": "X", "text": "second", "times": 1}`.
- Order: runtime rules first, in the order added, then the config rules. First match wins, so a runtime rule with the same `match` as a config rule replaces it until removed.
- `PATCH /admin/chaos` changes only the keys sent. Values are held to the config file's limits (see Chaos): `enabled` a JSON boolean, `frequency` an integer ≥ 1, `mode` `every`/`random`, `status` an integer 400–599, `kind` one of the four kinds, `afterChunks` an integer ≥ 0. Strings such as `"true"` or `"429"` are refused. Unknown keys are refused.
- `PATCH /admin/chaos` does not touch the call count. For a known failing call with `mode: "every"`: `POST /admin/reset`, then `PATCH /admin/chaos`; the count then starts at 0 (with `frequency: 2` the 1st call succeeds and the 2nd fails). `stats.calls` only counts calls made while chaos is enabled.
- `PATCH /admin/delay`: `min` and `max` are integers from 0 to 2147483647 and the resulting `min` must not exceed `max` (a key not sent keeps its value), so send both when raising the delay from `0`/`0`.
- `PATCH /admin/settings` changes only the keys sent, with the preset's names and JSON types: `responseType` `"lorem"`/`"stored"`, `maxLoremParas` an integer 1–1000, `stream`/`validateRequests`/`logRequests` JSON booleans (not `"ON"`/`"true"`), `maxLoggedRequests` an integer 1–100. Unknown keys are refused. `"stored"` uses the preset's `storedResponsesFile`, or the bundled texts if it has none; an unreadable file → `400`. `stream` is ignored by the `claude` template (the request's own `stream` decides). Not changeable while running: preset, template (`name`), `model`, `endpoint`, `embeddings`, `debug`, `storedResponsesFile`, port and host.
- A change applies from the next request. `GET /ui-meta` reports the settings in use.
- Send `POST /admin/rules` and the `PATCH` routes with `Content-Type: application/json`. Send the routes that take no body without a body.
- An `id` is never reused, also after a reset. Config rules have `id: null` and can not be removed.
- `POST /admin/reset` also drops connections a `stream-stall` is holding open. It does not touch the request log.
- The state is per server process and shared by every client: tests that add rules to one server must not run in parallel against it unless their `match` strings differ.
- Off with `"server": {"admin": false}` or `--admin=false` (the routes then 404); `0`, `off` and `no` are read as `false`, in any case. `GET /ui-meta` → `adminApi` is `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`. While it is on, a preset `endpoint` equal to `admin` or starting with `admin/` → startup error. No auth, like the rest of the server: use `server.host` `127.0.0.1` to keep it off the network.

Per-test fixture (any runner):

```js
const mock = 'http://localhost:8001';
const addRule = (rule) =>
  fetch(`${mock}/admin/rules`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(rule),
  });

beforeEach(() => fetch(`${mock}/admin/reset`, { method: 'POST' }));

test('high priority tickets are escalated', async () => {
  await addRule({ match: 'Classify this ticket', text: '{"priority":"high"}' });
  // ...call the code under test, which calls the mock...
});
```

## Stored replies (`storedResponsesFile`)

The way to get varied but realistic output: a pool of your own texts, one picked at random per request.

- Only used when `responseType` is `"stored"`. A matching `responseRules` entry still wins; the pool is the reply for everything no rule matches.
- The file is a JSON array of strings: `["first reply", "second reply"]`. Entries may also be objects with a string `content` (`[{ "id": 1, "content": "..." }]`, the shape of the bundled data; other keys are ignored).
- The path resolves relative to the folder containing the config file.
- Empty/non-string path → server refuses to start. With `responseType: "stored"`, a file that is missing, unreadable, not valid JSON, not an array, empty, or has an entry of another shape → server refuses to start.
- The file is checked at startup and re-read on every request, so editing it needs no restart. If it becomes invalid while the server runs, requests get `500` (no fallback to the bundled strings).
- Unset → the bundled strings are used.
- GET requests to the chat route also reply from the pool (only rules need a body).
- `GET /ui-meta` → `storedResponsesCount` is the size of the pool in use and `storedResponsesFile` its configured path (`null` = bundled strings; both `null` unless `responseType` is `"stored"`).
- `GET /ui-stored-responses` → `{"file", "responses": [...]}`: every text in the pool in use.

## Validation

With `validateRequests: true`, a POST body must be a JSON object containing these **top-level keys** (presence only; values and extra keys are not checked):

| `name` | Required keys |
|---|---|
| `openai` | `model`, `messages` |
| `claude` | `model`, `max_tokens`, `messages` |
| `gemini` | `contents` |
| embeddings route (any preset) | `model`, `input` |

Failure → `400 text/plain` (the message names the preset, not the missing key; the detail is at `GET /ui-request-log`). The required keys are the top-level keys of the request template, so a project template changes them.

## Responses

**OpenAI format** (`name: "openai"`), non-streaming:
`{"id","object":"chat.completion","created","model","usage":{…},"choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"<text>"},"finish_reason":"stop","index":0}]}`. `id`, `created`, `model` (`gpt-3.5-turbo-0301`) and `usage` (12/99/111) are constants; the request's `model` is not echoed.

Streaming is decided by the preset's `stream` setting only; the request's `stream` field is ignored. So a client that sends `stream: true` to a non-streaming preset receives plain JSON, and vice versa: keep the two in agreement. Stream shape: `data: {chat.completion.chunk}` lines — one role delta, then content deltas (which concatenate to the exact text), then an empty delta with `finish_reason: "stop"`, then `data: [DONE]`.

**Claude format** (`name: "claude"`), non-streaming:
`{"id":"msg_<random>","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"<request model>","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<text>"}],"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":0}}`. Token counts are estimates (~4 chars per token).

Streaming is per request: SSE if and only if the body has `"stream": true`. Events, in order: `message_start`, `content_block_start`, `content_block_delta` × n (`text_delta`, concatenating to the exact text), `content_block_stop`, `message_delta` (`stop_reason: "end_turn"`), `message_stop`. Always one text block.

**Gemini format** (`name: "gemini"`): `{"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"text":"<text>"}],"role":"model"},"finishReason":"STOP","index":0,"safetyRatings":[…]}]}`. With `stream: true` the output is OpenAI-style chunks, not Gemini's stream format.

**Stop reasons**: a reply produced by a response rule with `stopReason` ends with the value below, streamed or not. Every other reply ends as shown above.

| `stopReason` | `claude` | `openai` and custom names | `gemini` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `end` (default) | `stop_reason: "end_turn"` | `finish_reason: "stop"` | `finishReason: "STOP"` |
| `max_tokens` | `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` | `finish_reason: "length"` | `finishReason: "MAX_TOKENS"` |
| `refusal` | `stop_reason: "refusal"` | `finish_reason: "content_filter"` | `finishReason: "SAFETY"` |

- Streamed: `claude` carries it in the `message_delta` event's `delta`; the OpenAI-style stream in the final chunk's `finish_reason`. A streamed `gemini` or custom reply is OpenAI-style, so it gets the `openai` value.
- `claude` with `refusal` also sends Anthropic's `stop_details`: `{"type":"refusal","category":null,"explanation":null}`, top-level in the message and inside `delta` of `message_delta`. `category` and `explanation` are always `null` (the API's value for a refusal with no named policy area). No other reply has a `stop_details` key (the real API sends `stop_details: null` there).
- With `end` or no `stopReason` the response template's own value is kept, so a project template that sets another one still wins. A custom template with no `choices` list has nowhere to carry the value when not streamed.

**Embeddings** (`POST /v1/embeddings`, body `{"model","input": string | string[], "dimensions"?}`):
`{"object":"list","data":[{"object":"embedding","index":0,"embedding":[…]}],"model":"<request model>","usage":{"prompt_tokens","total_tokens"}}`. Vectors are deterministic for a given (`model`, input) pair, values in [-1, 1], not normalised and not semantic: similarity between them is meaningless. Request `dimensions` overrides the configured size.

**Timing**: every reply waits a random `responseDelay` first. Streams then add at least 50 ms between events, even with delay `0`/`0`, so a streamed reply takes roughly 0.5 s minimum.

## Chaos (`chaos`)

The way to test retries, backoff and error handling: some calls fail. By default a failing call gets an HTTP error in place of a reply; `chaos.kind` makes it a stream that fails part-way through instead.

- Off unless `chaos.enabled` is true (or `--chaos=true`). Example: `"chaos": { "enabled": true, "frequency": 3, "mode": "every", "status": 429 }` fails calls 3, 6, 9… with a 429.
- Use `mode: "every"` for deterministic tests: the count starts at 0 when the server starts, so with `frequency: 2` the 1st call succeeds and the 2nd fails. `frequency: 1` fails every call. `mode: "random"` fails each call with probability 1/`frequency`.
- One count is shared by the chat route (POST and GET) and `/v1/embeddings`. `/ping`, `/` and the `/ui-*` routes never fail and are not counted. A request that fails validation gets its usual `400` and is not counted.
- The `responseDelay` wait happens first. With `kind: "http"` a failing call that asked for a stream gets the JSON error, not SSE.
- Error body by preset `name` (`kind: "http"`):
  - `openai` and custom names: `{"error":{"message","type","param":null,"code"}}`; `type` is `rate_limit_error` (`code` `rate_limit_exceeded`) for 429, else `server_error` (`code` `null`).
  - `claude`: `{"type":"error","error":{"type","message"}}`; `type` is `rate_limit_error` (429), `overloaded_error` (529), else `api_error`.
  - `gemini`: `{"error":{"code":<status>,"message","status"}}`; `status` is `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (429), `UNAVAILABLE` (503), else `INTERNAL`.
  - `/v1/embeddings` always uses the `openai` shape.
- Headers: every chaos error has `x-llmock-chaos: true`; 429, 503 and 529 also have `retry-after: 1`.
- `chaos.kind` decides what a failing call gets. `frequency` and `mode` still decide which calls fail, with the same shared count:

  | `kind` | A failing call that asked for a stream | A failing call that did not |
  |---|---|---|
  | `http` (default) | The HTTP error above | The HTTP error above |
  | `stream-error` | Stream starts, `afterChunks` content deltas, then the in-stream error, then the response ends | The HTTP error above |
  | `stream-drop` | Stream starts, `afterChunks` content deltas, then the socket is destroyed | The socket is destroyed with no response |
  | `stream-stall` | Stream starts, `afterChunks` content deltas, then nothing; the connection stays open until the client disconnects | No response; the connection stays open until the client disconnects |

- A stream that fails has status `200` and the header `x-llmock-chaos: true` (the headers go out before the failure, so there is no `retry-after`), sends its opening events and deltas as usual, and never sends its closing events: no `content_block_stop`, `message_delta` or `message_stop` for `claude`; no `finish_reason` chunk and no `data: [DONE]` for the OpenAI-style stream.
- `afterChunks` (default 2) counts content deltas: `content_block_delta` events for `claude`, content chunks for the OpenAI-style stream. `0` fails straight after the opening events (`message_start` + `content_block_start`, or the role chunk). A reply with fewer deltas than `afterChunks` fails after its last delta. A reply is split into about 5 deltas, so use a fixture of several words to have something to cut.
- The in-stream error of `stream-error`:
  - `claude`: the SSE event `event: error` with `data: {"type":"error","error":{"type","message"}}`. `type` follows `chaos.status` as in the HTTP error (429 `rate_limit_error`, 529 `overloaded_error`, else `api_error`); `message` is `llmock chaos: simulated <status> error`.
  - OpenAI-style stream (`openai`, `gemini` and custom names): a `data:` line holding the `openai` error body above (also for `gemini`).
- Whether a call "asked for a stream" follows the usual rule: the request's `stream: true` for `claude`, the preset's `stream` setting for the others. `/v1/embeddings` never streams, so it takes the right-hand column.
- `stream-stall` sends no keep-alive and never times out on the server side: set a timeout in the client under test. Stalled connections are dropped when the server stops, so `stop` and a `SIGTERM` still work.
- In the config file, a `frequency` that is not an integer ≥ 1, a `mode` other than `every`/`random`, a `status` outside 400–599, an unknown `kind`, or an `afterChunks` that is not an integer ≥ 0 → server refuses to start. An invalid CLI flag value falls back to the default instead.
- `GET /ui-meta` → `chaosStatus` (`ENABLED`/`DISABLED`), `chaosFrequency`, `chaosMode`, `chaosErrorStatus`, `chaosKind`, `chaosAfterChunks`, and `chaosInjected` (failures of any kind since startup).
- Not simulated: a malformed HTTP response (for bad JSON inside the reply text, write a broken fixture), a reply that arrives late but whole (use `responseDelay`), and a failure on only some of the calls that match a prompt. To fail every call that matches a prompt, and no other, use a response rule with `fail` (see Fixture replies).

## Custom formats (templates)

To change a response envelope or the required request keys, or to mock a provider with another JSON shape, add templates beside `.llmockrc.json`:

- `request-templates/<name>_req.json`: `[ { …example request… } ]`. Its top-level keys become the required keys.
- `response-templates/<name>_res.json`: `[ { …response… } ]`. Every string value equal to `DYNAMIC_CONTENT_HERE` is replaced by the reply text.

`<name>` is the preset's `name`. Both files are a JSON array whose first element is used. A project file overrides the built-in one of the same name (`openai`, `gemini`, `claude`); templates are read per request. A custom `name` needs the response template always, and the request template when `validateRequests` is true. Custom formats stream as OpenAI-style chunks. Scaffolded projects already contain editable copies of the built-in templates. In Docker, mount or copy both folders next to the config.

## Other routes

| Route | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /ping` | `{"response":"server is running"}` |
| `GET /ui-meta` | Active settings as JSON |
| `GET /ui-stored-responses` | The stored responses pool in use, as JSON |
| `GET /ui-rule-file?rule=<i>&file=<j>` | Contents of one response rule file, as JSON |
| `GET /ui-request-log` | `{"file", "log"}`: `log` is an array of the most recent validated requests (the last `maxLoggedRequests`, 10 by default), newest first, each with why it passed/failed (older ones are dropped; `log` is `null` if none logged) |
| `DELETE /ui-request-log` | Empties the request log; returns `{"file", "log": null}` |
| `/admin/rules`, `/admin/chaos`, `/admin/delay`, `/admin/settings`, `/admin/reset` | Change response rules, chaos, delay and reply settings while running (see Admin API) |
| `GET /` | HTML dashboard |
| `GET /<endpoint>` | A generated reply with no validation and no rules (quick smoke test) |

## Limits to design around

- CORS: only streamed replies carry `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, and there is no `OPTIONS` handler. Browser code calling the mock cross-origin will fail preflight; call it from a server/test process or through your dev-server proxy.
- Not mocked: tool/function calls, images, multiple choices (`n`), the stop reasons `tool_use`, `stop_sequence` and `pause_turn` (and their equivalents in the other formats), `/v1/models`, `/v1/messages/count_tokens`.

## Recipes

Test setup (any runner):

```js
import { execSync } from 'node:child_process';

export function startMock() {
  // Returns once the server answers; throws if it could not start
  execSync('npx llmock start --model=claude --port=8001', { stdio: 'inherit' });
}
export const stopMock = () => execSync('npx llmock stop --port=8001');
```

Fast deterministic tests: `"responseDelay": {"min": 0, "max": 0}`, one `responseRules` entry per scenario keyed on a unique marker string in the prompt. Or keep each scenario's reply next to its test: `POST /admin/rules` in the test, `POST /admin/reset` in `beforeEach` (see Admin API).

Retry tests: `"chaos": {"enabled": true, "frequency": 2, "status": 429}` makes every 2nd call fail, so a client that retries once always succeeds. Run it as its own preset (or with `--chaos=true`) so other tests are unaffected, or switch it on for one test with `PATCH /admin/chaos` and `POST /admin/reset` afterwards (see Admin API).

Mid-stream failure tests: `"chaos": {"enabled": true, "frequency": 1, "kind": "stream-error", "afterChunks": 1}` on a `claude` preset (or `--chaos=true --chaosKind=stream-error --chaosAfterChunks=1`) makes every streamed call start, send one delta, then fail. With the Anthropic SDK the stream throws:

```js
const stream = client.messages.stream({ model: 'claude-opus-5-5', max_tokens: 256, messages });
await expect(stream.finalMessage()).rejects.toThrow(); // an APIError carrying the overloaded_error body
```

Use `stream-drop` to test a connection cut with no error event, and `stream-stall` (with a short timeout on the client) to test a reply that hangs. Set `frequency: 2` to let a client that retries once succeed. Keep the SDK's own retries in mind (`maxRetries: 0` to see the first failure).

Failing one prompt and not the rest: `"responseRules": [{ "match": "<text only that prompt has>", "fail": { "kind": "stream-drop" } }]`. No `chaos` needed, and the tests around it do not depend on call order.

Truncated or refused replies: a rule with `"stopReason": "max_tokens"` (or `"refusal"`) and a fixture that reads like one, then assert your code checks the stop reason before using the text.

Varied replies: `"responseType": "stored"` with `"storedResponsesFile": "fixtures/replies.json"` for every unmatched request, or a rule with `files` for one kind of request. Assert on membership of the pool, not on one exact text.

Docker (config and fixtures mounted, no rebuild on change):

```dockerfile
FROM node:24-alpine
WORKDIR /app
RUN npm install --omit=dev llmock
EXPOSE 8001
CMD ["npx", "llmock", "start", "--foreground"]
```

Mount `.llmockrc.json` to `/app/.llmockrc.json`, with the fixtures folder (and any template folders) beside it. A `storedResponsesFile` must be mounted too, at the same path relative to the config (simplest: keep it inside the fixtures folder). `--foreground` is required or the container exits.
